# Whether a point is a member of a ball, one-limb center

Kernel `ball_contains_point_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether the point $t$ is a finite number and a member of $X$, $X$ the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies t \in X.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c$ and radius $r$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $t$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when the point $t$ is a finite number and a member of $X$: the answer is exact.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked. The [Proofs](../proofs/index.md#what-is-proved-and-in-which-model) page says which statements of the IEEE model are proved against statements written by hand; this page gives the status that `gen/claims.json` gives.

## Source

**Algorithm:** the distance as an exact pair compared with the radius (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_contains_point_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_contains_point_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum_ord`](two_sum_ord.md), [`abs_2`](abs_2.md), [`le_2_1`](le_2_1.md).

```
# Whether a value t of T is a member of a ball with a one-limb center (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", the row of contains(t), "Exact pairs"): |t - c| <= r, decided exactly as
# le_2_1(abs_2(two_sum_ord(t, -c)), r), the difference being an exact pair. A difference that
# overflows is (+inf, -inf), which le_2_1 calls above every radius, the right answer: it exceeds
# Omega. The whole line, (0, +inf), contains every finite t; the empty set (NaN, NaN) and a t that
# is not finite give false, through the same operations. t is a value of the program, guarded before
# the sum (rule R3). Exact.

g        = guard(t)
nc       = neg(c)
(d0, d1) = two_sum_ord(g, nc)
(a0, a1) = abs_2(d0, d1)
m        = le_2_1(a0, a1, r)
```
